task_instance: Package a sample support issue (Acme Corp Enterprise account seeing intermittent 500 errors on the /v2/orders export API, with 2 similar reports from other customers) into a structured escalation brief: assess business impact, pick severity and escalation target, write reproduction steps, and render the full ESCALATION brief using the skill's template.
evidence: Created support_tickets.json (a local stand-in for the 'support platform' data source the skill normally pulls from via connectors) describing one primary ticket plus 2 similar reports. Wrote generate_escalation.py which implements the skill's steps 3-6 in code: computes breadth/depth/duration/revenue/time-pressure impact dimensions, applies the SKILL.md severity rule (pattern of 3+ customers + Enterprise account blocked => Critical), picks escalation target (Engineering for the confirmed, reproduced bug; cc Leadership for the revenue-at-risk/churn-threat angle per the 'Any -> Leadership' tier), derives reproduction steps/expected/actual/environment from the ticket's troubleshooting and evidence fields, and renders the exact ESCALATION brief template from SKILL.md into escalation_brief.md. Ran `python3 generate_escalation.py` successfully (see stdout) and verified escalation_brief.md exists (3335 bytes) and contains every required template section (## ESCALATION, ### Impact, ### Issue Description, ### What's Been Tried, ### Reproduction Steps, ### Customer Communication, ### What's Needed, ### Supporting Context) via grep, all passing. No network access, external connectors, or credentials were needed since the skill's connector-backed context sources (support platform, CRM, chat, project tracker, knowledge base) are explicitly optional ('if connected') and the core deliverable -- synthesizing available ticket data into a structured escalation brief -- is a pure text-generation task achievable entirely offline with local sample data.
